sentences.zh: 魏允貞

translations.literal: Wei Yunzhen
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yunzhen

sentences.zh: （弟允中劉廷蘭）〉

translations.literal: (his younger brother Yunzhong and Liu Tinglan)
translations.idiomatic: (his younger brother Yunzhong and Liu Tinglan)

sentences.zh: 王國余懋衡李三才

translations.literal: Wang Guo, Yu Maohéng, and Li Sancai
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo, Yu Maohéng, and Li Sancai

sentences.zh: 魏允貞，字懋忠，南樂人。

translations.literal: Wei Yunzhen, styled Maozhong, was a native of Nanle.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yunzhen, whose style was Maozhong, came from Nanle.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Wanli reign (1577).

sentences.zh: 授荊州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大學士張居正歸葬，群吏趨事恐後，允貞獨不赴，且抶其奴。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng returned home for his father's funeral, the whole corps of officials rushed to serve him in fear of falling behind, but Yunzhen alone did not go, and even beat Zhang's servant.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng went home to bury his father, officials everywhere scrambled to attend him, but Yunzhen alone stayed away and even had Zhang's servant beaten.

sentences.zh: 治行最，征授御史。

translations.literal: His administration ranked first, and he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: His record of governance ranked first, and he was summoned to serve as a censor.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書梁夢龍罷。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Liang Menglong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Liang Menglong was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 允貞言：「銓衡任重。

translations.literal: Yunzhen said: "The power of appointment weighs heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen said, "The power to appoint officials carries great weight.

sentences.zh: 往者會推之前，所司率受指執政或司禮中官，以故用非其人。

translations.literal: Before each joint recommendation, the responsible offices invariably took orders from the chief minister or from the Directorate eunuchs, and thus men unfit for office were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Before each joint recommendation, the responsible offices invariably took instructions from the chief minister or from eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonial, and for that reason unworthy men were appointed.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言，特用嚴清，中外翕服。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and specially appointed Yan Qing; within and without the court all were united in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice and specially appointed Yan Qing; inside and outside the court all were won over.

sentences.zh: 俄劾兵部尚書吳兌，兌引去。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Minister of War Wu Dui, who withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he impeached Minister of War Wu Dui, who resigned.

sentences.zh: 已，陳時弊四事，言：「自居正竊柄，吏、兵二部遷除必先關白，故所用悉其私人。

translations.literal: Thereafter he presented four current abuses, saying: "Since Juzheng seized power, transfers in the Ministries of Personnel and War had first to be reported to him, so those appointed were all his private connections.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he presented four abuses of the age, saying, "Since Juzheng monopolized power, every transfer in the Ministries of Personnel and War had to be reported to him first, so those appointed were all his private connections.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜與輔臣精察二部之長，而以其職事歸之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should together with the assistant ministers carefully scrutinize the heads of the two ministries and restore their proper duties to them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should work with the grand secretaries to scrutinize closely the heads of the two ministries and restore their proper duties to them.

sentences.zh: 使輔臣不侵部臣之權以行其私，部臣亦不乘輔臣之間以自行其私，則官方自肅。

translations.literal: If assistant ministers do not infringe the authority of ministry heads to pursue private ends, and ministry heads likewise do not take advantage of gaps among the assistants to pursue their own private ends, then official discipline will of itself be restored.
translations.idiomatic: If grand secretaries do not infringe on ministry heads' authority to pursue private ends, and ministry heads do not exploit gaps among the grand secretaries to pursue their own private ends, then official discipline will restore itself.

sentences.zh: 自居正三子連登制科，流弊迄今未已。

translations.literal: Since Juzheng's three sons passed the palace examination in succession, the ill effects continue down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Since Juzheng's three sons passed the palace examination in succession, the abuses continue down to the present day.

sentences.zh: 請自今輔臣子弟中式，俟致政之後始許廷對，庶幸門稍杜。

translations.literal: I beg that from now on when sons of assistant ministers pass the provincial examinations, they be allowed to take the palace examination only after their fathers have retired, so that the door of favoritism may be somewhat shut.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that from now on, when sons of grand secretaries pass the provincial examinations, they be allowed to take the palace examination only after their fathers have retired from office, so that the door of favoritism may be somewhat closed.

sentences.zh: 自居正惡聞讜言，每遇科道員缺，率擇才性便給、工諂媚、善逢迎者授之，致昌言不聞，佞臣得誌。

translations.literal: Since Juzheng hated to hear frank criticism, whenever a vacancy arose among the censorate and surveillance commissioners, he invariably chose men of nimble talent, skilled in flattery, adept at currying favor, so that forthright speech was not heard and fawning ministers had their way.
translations.idiomatic: Since Juzheng hated to hear frank criticism, whenever a vacancy arose among the censorate and surveillance commissioners, he invariably chose men who were quick-witted, skilled at flattery, and adept at currying favor, so that forthright speech was not heard and fawning ministers had their way.

sentences.zh: 自今考選時，陛下宜嚴敕所司，毋循故轍。

translations.literal: From this examination onward, Your Majesty should strictly charge the responsible offices not to follow the old rut.
translations.idiomatic: From this selection onward, Your Majesty should strictly charge the responsible offices not to follow the old rut.

sentences.zh: 俺答自通市以來，邊備懈弛。

translations.literal: Since Altan began border trade, border defenses have grown lax.
translations.idiomatic: Since Altan opened border trade, frontier defenses have grown lax.

sentences.zh: 三軍月餉，既克其半以充市賞，復克其半以奉要人，士無宿飽，何能禦寇？

translations.literal: Of the army's monthly stipends, half is already withheld for market rewards, and half of what remains is again withheld for powerful men; the soldiers have no full stores, how can they repel the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Half of the army's monthly pay is already withheld for market rewards, and half of what remains is again withheld for powerful men; the troops have no stores from one day to the next — how can they repel the enemy?

sentences.zh: 至遼左戰功，尤可駭異。

translations.literal: As for military achievements on the eastern frontier, they are especially startling and strange.
translations.idiomatic: As for military achievements on the eastern frontier, they are especially startling and strange.

sentences.zh: 軍聲則日振於前，生齒則日減於舊。

translations.literal: Military reports grow louder day by day, while population figures shrink daily from old levels.
translations.idiomatic: Battle reports grow louder by the day, while population figures shrink daily from what they once were.

sentences.zh: 奏報失真，遷敘逾格，賞罰無章，何以能國哉！

translations.literal: Memorials distort the truth, promotions and rewards exceed proper bounds, and rewards and punishments lack rule — how can such a state endure!
translations.idiomatic: Memorials distort the truth, promotions and rewards exceed proper bounds, and rewards and punishments lack rule — how can such a state endure!

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下都察院。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was sent down to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, it was sent down to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 先是，居正既私其子，他輔臣呂調陽子興周，張四維子泰徵、甲徵，申時行子用懋，皆相繼得舉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Juzheng had already favored his sons; other assistant ministers' sons — Lü Tiaoyang's son Xingzhou, Zhang Siwei's sons Taizheng and Jiazheng, Shen Shixing's son Yongmao — had in succession all passed examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Juzheng had already favored his own sons; the sons of other grand secretaries — Lü Tiaoyang's son Xingzhou, Zhang Siwei's sons Taizheng and Jiazheng, and Shen Shixing's son Yongmao — had in succession all passed the examinations.

sentences.zh: 甲徵、用懋將廷對，而允貞疏適上。

translations.literal: Jiazheng and Yongmao were about to take the palace examination when Yunzhen's memorial arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazheng and Yongmao were about to take the palace examination when Yunzhen's memorial arrived.

sentences.zh: 四維大慍，言：「臣待罪政府，無所不當聞。

translations.literal: Siwei was greatly angered and said: "Your servant holds office in the government and ought to hear of everything.
translations.idiomatic: Siwei was greatly angered and said, "Your servant holds office in the government and ought to hear of everything.

sentences.zh: 今因前人行私，而欲臣不預聞吏、兵二部事，非制也。

translations.literal: Now because former men pursued private ends, you wish your servant not to be informed beforehand of matters in the Ministries of Personnel and War — this is not the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Now because former men pursued private ends, you wish your servant not to be informed beforehand of matters in the Ministries of Personnel and War — this is not the regulation.

sentences.zh: 」因為子白誣，且乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He therefore pled innocence for his son and begged to resign his bones.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore pled innocence for his son and begged to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 時行亦疏辨。

translations.literal: Shixing also submitted a defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing also submitted a defense.

sentences.zh: 帝並慰留，而責允貞言過當。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled both and kept them, but reproved Yunzhen for speaking excessively.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consoled both and kept them in office, but reproved Yunzhen for speaking excessively.

sentences.zh: 戶部員外郎李三才奏允貞言是，並貶秩調外。

translations.literal: Junior Department Director Li Sancai memorialized that Yunzhen was right, and both were demoted in rank and transferred outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Department Director Li Sancai memorialized that Yunzhen was right, and both were demoted in rank and transferred outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 允貞得許州判官。

translations.literal: Yunzhen received appointment as vice magistrate of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen was appointed vice magistrate of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中御史周邦傑、趙卿等論救，不納。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors Zhou Bangjie, Zhao Qing, and others memorialized in his defense, but this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors Zhou Bangjie, Zhao Qing, and others memorialized in his defense, but this was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 允貞雖謫，然自是輔臣居位，其子無復登第者。

translations.literal: Though Yunzhen was banished, from this time forward while assistant ministers held office their sons no longer passed examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yunzhen was banished, from this time forward, while grand secretaries held office, their sons no longer passed the examinations.

sentences.zh: 久之，累遷右通政。

translations.literal: After a long while he was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Commissioner of Transport.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was repeatedly promoted until he became Right Vice Commissioner of Transport.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以右僉都御史巡撫山西。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1593) he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 允貞素剛果，清操絕俗。

translations.literal: Yunzhen had always been firm and resolute, with purity of conduct beyond the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen had always been firm and resolute, with a purity of conduct beyond the common run.

sentences.zh: 以所部地疹民貧，力裁幕府歲供及州縣冗費，以其銀數萬繕亭障，建烽堠，置器市馬易粟。

translations.literal: Because the territory under his charge was barren and the people poor, he strenuously cut the annual supplies of the military establishment and redundant expenditures of prefectures and counties, and with the several tens of thousands in silver thus saved repaired barrier posts, built beacon towers, procured weapons, bought horses, and exchanged grain.
translations.idiomatic: Because the territory under his charge was barren and the people poor, he strenuously cut the military establishment's annual supplies and redundant expenditures of prefectures and counties, and with the several tens of thousands in silver thus saved repaired barrier posts, built beacon towers, procured weapons, bought horses, and exchanged grain.

sentences.zh: 又奏免平陽歲額站銀八萬，以所省郵傳羨補之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized exemption of the eighty thousand taels of annual station silver for Pingyang, using surplus from post relays to make up the difference.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized exemption of the eighty thousand taels of annual station silver for Pingyang, using surplus from the post relay system to make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 雁門、平定軍以逋屯糧竄徙，允貞奏除其租，招令復業。

translations.literal: Armies at Yanmen and Pingding had fled because of arrears in colony grain; Yunzhen memorialized to remit their rent and summoned them back to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: The armies at Yanmen and Pingding had scattered because of arrears in colony grain; Yunzhen memorialized to remit their rent and summoned them back to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 岢嵐互市，省撫賞銀六萬。

translations.literal: At the Kola mutual market he saved sixty thousand taels in frontier reward silver.
translations.idiomatic: At the Kola mutual market he saved sixty thousand taels in frontier reward silver.

sentences.zh: 汾州有兩郡王，宗人與軍民雜處，知州秩卑不能制，奏改為府。

translations.literal: Fenzhou had two imperial princes of the second rank, and clansmen were mixed with soldiers and civilians; the prefect's rank was too low to control them, so he memorialized to change it to a superior prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fenzhou had two commandery princes, and clansmen were mixed with soldiers and civilians; the prefect's rank was too low to control them, so he memorialized to elevate it to a superior prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自款市成，邊政廢。

translations.literal: Since the pacification market was established, frontier administration had fallen into decay.
translations.idiomatic: Since the pacification market was established, frontier administration had fallen into decay.

sentences.zh: 允貞視要害，築邊墻萬有余丈。

translations.literal: Yunzhen surveyed strategic points and built more than ten thousand feet of border wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen surveyed strategic points and built more than ten thousand feet of border wall.

sentences.zh: 政聲大著。

translations.literal: His administrative reputation grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation for governance grew greatly.

sentences.zh: 帝亦數嘉其能。

translations.literal: The emperor also repeatedly praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also repeatedly praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 會詔中官張忠采礦山西，允貞抗疏極諫，不報。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict ordered the eunuch Zhang Zhong to open mining in Shanxi; Yunzhen submitted a forceful memorial in extreme remonstrance, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that an edict ordered the eunuch Zhang Zhong to open mines in Shanxi; Yunzhen submitted a forceful memorial in extreme remonstrance, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 已，西河王知燧請開解州、安邑、絳縣礦，以儀賓督之。

translations.literal: Later Prince of Xihe Zhizhui requested opening mines in Jiezhou, Anyi, and Jiangxian, to be supervised by his ceremonial son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Xihe, Zhizhui, requested opening mines in Jiezhou, Anyi, and Jiangxian, to be supervised by his ceremonial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 指揮王守信請開平定、稷山諸礦。

translations.literal: Commander Wang Shouxin requested opening mines in Pingding, Jishan, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wang Shouxin requested opening mines in Pingding, Jishan, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 帝並報允。

translations.literal: The emperor approved both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved both requests.

sentences.zh: 允貞恐民愈擾，請令忠兼領，亦不納。

translations.literal: Yunzhen feared the people would be disturbed still more and requested that Zhong be put in overall charge, but this too was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen feared the people would be disturbed still more and requested that Zhong be put in overall charge, but this too was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 三殿災，詔求直言。

translations.literal: When the three main halls burned, an edict sought forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: When the three main halls burned, an edict sought forthright speech.

sentences.zh: 允貞言咎在輔臣，歷數趙誌臯、張位罪。

translations.literal: Yunzhen said the blame lay with the assistant ministers, enumerating the offenses of Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen said the blame lay with the grand secretaries and enumerated the offenses of Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「前二臣以二月加恩，逾月兩宮災。

translations.literal: And he said: "The former two ministers received favors in the second month, and within a month both palaces suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The former two ministers received favors in the second month, and within a month both palaces suffered disaster.

sentences.zh: 今年又加恩，而三殿復災。

translations.literal: This year favors were granted again, and the three halls again burned.
translations.idiomatic: This year favors were granted again, and the three halls again burned.

sentences.zh: 天意昭然。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent is clear."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent is clear."

sentences.zh: 」位等力辨，求罷。

translations.literal: Wei and the others argued forcefully and begged dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and the others argued forcefully and begged to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留，責允貞邊臣不當言朝事，因屢推不用，遂肆狂言，奪俸五月。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled and kept them, reproving Yunzhen that border officials ought not speak of court affairs; because he had repeatedly been passed over for use he had let loose wild talk — five months' salary was docked.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consoled and kept them in office, reproving Yunzhen that frontier officials ought not speak of court affairs; because he had repeatedly been passed over for appointment he had let loose wild talk — five months' salary was docked.

sentences.zh: 頃之，允貞疏舉遺賢，請召還王家屏、陳有年、沈鯉、李世達、王汝訓及小臣史孟麟、張棟、萬國欽、馬經綸、顧憲成、趙南星、鄒元標等，疏留中。

translations.literal: Before long Yunzhen memorialized recommending departed worthies, asking to recall Wang Jiaping, Chen Younian, Shen Li, Li Shida, Wang Ruxun, and junior officials Shi Menglin, Zhang Dong, Wan Guoqin, Ma Jinglun, Gu Xiancheng, Zhao Nanxing, Zou Yuanbiao, and others; the memorial was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yunzhen memorialized recommending departed worthies, asking to recall Wang Jiaping, Chen Younian, Shen Li, Li Shida, Wang Ruxun, and junior officials Shi Menglin, Zhang Dong, Wan Guoqin, Ma Jinglun, Gu Xiancheng, Zhao Nanxing, Zou Yuanbiao, and others; the memorial was kept at court.

sentences.zh: 以久次，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: Because of long tenure he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Because of long tenure he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二十八年春，疏陳時政缺失，言：「行取諸臣，幾經論薦，陛下猶不輕予一官。

translations.literal: In spring of the twenty-eighth year he memorialized on current governmental deficiencies, saying: "The various officials selected for promotion have been recommended again and again in discussion, yet Your Majesty still will not lightly grant a single post.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the twenty-eighth year (1600) he memorialized on current governmental deficiencies, saying, "The various officials selected for promotion have been recommended again and again in discussion, yet Your Majesty still will not lightly grant a single post.

sentences.zh: 彼魯坤、馬堂、高淮、陳朝輩，試之何事，舉之何人，乃令其銜命橫行，生殺予奪，恣出其口。

translations.literal: Yet Lu Kun, Ma Tang, Gao Huai, Chen Chao, and their like — what were they tested in, who recommended them — that they should bear orders and run rampant, holding life and death and reward and punishment at their lips as they please?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lu Kun, Ma Tang, Gao Huai, Chen Chao, and their like — what were they tested in, who recommended them — that they should bear orders and run rampant, holding life and death and reward and punishment on their lips as they please?

sentences.zh: 廷臣所陳率國家大計，一皆寢閣，甚者嚴譴隨之。

translations.literal: What court ministers present are invariably great plans of state, all shelved without exception, and in severe cases harsh censure follows at once.
translations.idiomatic: What court ministers present are invariably great plans of state, all shelved without exception, and in severe cases harsh censure follows at once.

sentences.zh: 彼報稅之徒，悉無賴奸人，鄉黨不齒，顧乃朝奏夕報，如響應聲。

translations.literal: Yet those who report taxes are all worthless rogues whom their native districts will not have — yet morning memorials receive evening responses, like echo answering sound.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who report taxes are all worthless rogues whom their native districts will not have — yet morning memorials receive evening responses, like echo answering sound.

sentences.zh: 臣不解也。

translations.literal: Your servant does not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant does not understand.

sentences.zh: 胥徒入鄉，民間猶擾，況緹騎四出，如虎若狼，家室立破。

translations.literal: When minor clerks enter the countryside the people are still disturbed; how much more when brocade-clad guards go forth on four sides like tigers and wolves, and households are ruined at once?
translations.idiomatic: When minor clerks enter the countryside the people are still disturbed; how much more when brocade-clad guards go forth on four sides like tigers and wolves, and households are ruined at once?

sentences.zh: 如吳寶秀、華鈺諸人，禍至慘矣，而陛下曾不一念及。

translations.literal: Men such as Wu Baoxiu and Hua Yu suffered to the bitter end, yet Your Majesty has never once given them a thought.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Wu Baoxiu and Hua Yu suffered to the bitter end, yet Your Majesty has never once given them a thought.

sentences.zh: 錢谷出入，上下相稽，猶多奸弊。

translations.literal: In the coming and going of money and grain, superiors and subordinates check each other, yet many corrupt practices remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the coming and going of money and grain, superiors and subordinates check each other, yet many corrupt practices remain.

sentences.zh: 敕使手握利權，動逾數萬。

translations.literal: Edict commissioners hold profit in their hands, each movement exceeding tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Edict commissioners hold profit in their hands, each transaction exceeding tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 有司不敢問，撫按不敢聞，豈無吮膏血以自肥者，而陛下曾不一察及。

translations.literal: Local officials dare not inquire, governors and surveillance commissioners dare not hear — can there be none who suck the people's blood to fatten themselves? Yet Your Majesty has never once investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials dare not inquire, governors and surveillance commissioners dare not hear — can there be none who suck the people's blood to fatten themselves? Yet Your Majesty has never once investigated.

sentences.zh: 金取於滇，不足不止；

translations.literal: Gold is taken from Yunnan — it does not stop until there is not enough;
translations.idiomatic: Gold is taken from Yunnan — it does not stop until there is not enough;

sentences.zh: 珠取於海，不罄不止；

translations.literal: Pearls are taken from the sea — they do not stop until none are left;
translations.idiomatic: Pearls are taken from the sea — they do not stop until none are left;

sentences.zh: 錦綺取於吳越，不極奇巧不止。

translations.literal: brocades and silks are taken from Wu and Yue — they do not stop until the utmost in bizarre craft is reached.
translations.idiomatic: Brocades and silks are taken from Wu and Yue — they do not stop until the utmost in bizarre craft is reached.

sentences.zh: 乃元老聽其投閑，直臣幾於永錮，是陛下之愛賢士，曾不如愛珠玉錦綺也。

translations.literal: Yet senior statesmen are left idle at their posts while upright ministers are nearly imprisoned forever — Your Majesty's love of worthy scholars falls short of love for pearls, jade, brocade, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yet senior statesmen are left idle while upright ministers are nearly imprisoned forever — Your Majesty's love of worthy scholars falls short of Your Majesty's love for pearls, jade, brocade, and silk.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，亦不省。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, again no notice was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, again no notice was taken.

sentences.zh: 先是，張忠以開礦至，後孫朝復至榷稅，誅求百方，允貞每事裁抑。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Zhong had come to open mines; later Sun Chao came to monopolize taxes, extorting by every means; Yunzhen checked each matter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Zhong had come to open mines; later Sun Chao came to monopolize taxes, extorting by every means; Yunzhen checked each matter.

sentences.zh: 會忠杖死太平典史武三傑，朝使者逼殺建雄縣丞李逢春，允貞疏暴其罪。

translations.literal: When Zhong beat to death the Taiping bureau clerk Wu Sanjie, and Chao's agents drove to suicide the Jianxiong county assistant Li Fengchun, Yunzhen memorialized exposing their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong beat to death the Taiping bureau clerk Wu Sanjie, and Chao's agents drove to suicide the Jianxiong county assistant Li Fengchun, Yunzhen memorialized exposing their crimes.

sentences.zh: 朝怒，劾允貞抗命沮撓。

translations.literal: Chao was angry and impeached Yunzhen for resisting orders and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was angry and impeached Yunzhen for resisting orders and obstruction.

sentences.zh: 帝留允貞疏不下，而下朝疏於部院。

translations.literal: The emperor kept Yunzhen's memorial from being sent down but sent down Chao's memorial to the ministries and the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept Yunzhen's memorial from being sent down but sent down Chao's memorial to the ministries and the censorate.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李戴、都御史溫純等力稱允貞賢，請下允貞疏平議。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Li Dai, Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun, and others strongly praised Yunzhen's worth and asked that Yunzhen's memorial be sent down for fair discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Li Dai, Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun, and others strongly praised Yunzhen's worth and asked that Yunzhen's memorial be sent down for fair discussion.

sentences.zh: 帝並留中。

translations.literal: The emperor kept both at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept both memorials at court.

sentences.zh: 山西軍民數千恐允貞去，相率詣闕訴冤，兩京言官亦連章論救。

translations.literal: Several thousand soldiers and civilians of Shanxi, fearing Yunzhen would leave, went together to the capital to plead their grievances; censors in both capitals also submitted linked memorials in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand soldiers and civilians of Shanxi, fearing Yunzhen would leave, went together to the capital to plead their grievances; censors in both capitals also submitted linked memorials in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝乃兩置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor then set both aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then set both aside without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 明年，忠以夏縣知縣彭應春抗禮，劾貶之。

translations.literal: The next year Zhong, because Xian county magistrate Peng Yingchun resisted his ceremonial precedence, impeached and demoted him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhong, because Xia county magistrate Peng Yingchun resisted his ceremonial precedence, impeached and demoted him.

sentences.zh: 允貞請留應春，不報。

translations.literal: Yunzhen asked to retain Yingchun; no response.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen asked to retain Yingchun; there was no response.

sentences.zh: 允貞父已九十余，允貞歲歲乞侍養，章二十上。

translations.literal: Yunzhen's father was already over ninety; year by year Yunzhen begged leave to attend him, memorializing twenty times.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen's father was already over ninety; year by year Yunzhen begged leave to attend him, memorializing twenty times.

sentences.zh: 廷議以敕使害民，非允貞不能制，固留之。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that the edict commissioners harmed the people and only Yunzhen could restrain them, so he was firmly kept.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion held that the edict commissioners harmed the people and only Yunzhen could restrain them, so he was firmly kept in office.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，請益力，始聽歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year he petitioned still more forcefully and was at last permitted to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year he petitioned still more forcefully and was at last permitted to return home.

sentences.zh: 士民為立祠。

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners erected a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners erected a shrine for him.

sentences.zh: 已，閱視者奏允貞守邊勞，即家進兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Later the inspection tour memorialized Yunzhen's labors on the frontier, and he was promoted at home to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Later the inspection tour memorialized Yunzhen's labors on the frontier, and he was promoted at home to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚介肅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously enfeoffed Jie Su.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously enfeoffed Jie Su.

sentences.zh: 弟允中、允孚。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Yunzhong and Yunfu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were Yunzhong and Yunfu.

sentences.zh: 允中為諸生，副使王世貞大器之。

translations.literal: Yunzhong was a licentiate; Vice Commissioner Wang Shizhen greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong was a licentiate; Vice Commissioner Wang Shizhen greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 歲鄉試，世貞戒門吏曰：「非魏允中第一，無伐鼓以傳也。

translations.literal: At the annual provincial examination, Shizhen warned the gate clerks: "Unless Wei Yunzhong ranks first, do not beat the drum to announce it.
translations.idiomatic: At the annual provincial examination, Shizhen warned the gate clerks, "Unless Wei Yunzhong ranks first, do not beat the drum to announce the results.

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: And so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 時無錫顧憲成、漳浦劉廷蘭並為舉首，負俊才，時人稱「三解元」。

translations.literal: At the time Gu Xiancheng of Wuxi and Liu Tinglan of Zhangpu were also provincial first-place graduates, all possessed of outstanding talent; people of the age called them the "Three Provincial Champions."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gu Xiancheng of Wuxi and Liu Tinglan of Zhangpu were also top graduates in the provincial examinations, all men of outstanding talent; contemporaries called them the "Three Provincial Champions."

sentences.zh: 尋與廷蘭舉萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he and Tinglan both passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he and Tinglan both received their jinshi degrees in the eighth year of the Wanli reign (1580).

sentences.zh: 張居正專政，災異見，而中外方競頌功德。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng monopolized government; omens and anomalies appeared, yet within and without the court all were competing to praise his merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng held sole power; portents and anomalies appeared, yet court and country alike were competing to praise his achievements.

sentences.zh: 允中、廷蘭各上書座主申時行，勸之補救。

translations.literal: Yunzhong and Tinglan each wrote to their patron Shen Shixing, urging remedial action.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong and Tinglan each wrote to their patron Shen Shixing, urging him to take remedial action.

sentences.zh: 時行不能用。

translations.literal: Shixing could not act on their advice.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing could not act on their advice.

sentences.zh: 允中尋授太常博士，擢吏部稽勛主事，調考功，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Yunzhong was soon appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Director of Records in the Ministry of Personnel, transferred to the Directorate of Evaluations, and died before long.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong was soon appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to Director of Records in the Ministry of Personnel, transferred to the Directorate of Evaluations, and died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 允孚官刑部郎中，亦有名。

translations.literal: Yunfu served as Director in the Ministry of Punishments and was also well known.
translations.idiomatic: Yunfu served as a director in the Ministry of Punishments and was likewise well known.

sentences.zh: 廷蘭與兄廷蕙、廷芥亦皆舉進士，有名。

translations.literal: Tinglan, together with his elder brothers Tinghui and Tingjie, all passed the metropolitan examination and were well known.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglan, together with his elder brothers Tinghui and Tingjie, all passed the metropolitan examination and won renown.

sentences.zh: 世所稱「南樂三魏」、「漳浦三劉」者也。

translations.literal: They are what the age called the "Three Wei of Nanle" and the "Three Liu of Zhangpu."
translations.idiomatic: They are what the age called the "Three Wei of Nanle" and the "Three Liu of Zhangpu."

sentences.zh: 王國，字子楨，耀州人。

translations.literal: Wang Guo, styled Zizhen, was a native of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo, whose style was Zizhen, came from Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Wanli reign (1577).

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，改御史。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and then transferred to serve as a censor.

sentences.zh: 出視畿輔屯田，清成國公朱允禎等所侵地九千六百余頃。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect metropolitan-area colony fields, he cleared more than nine thousand six hundred qing of land encroached upon by the Prince of Cheng Zhu Yunzhen and others.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out to inspect colony fields in the metropolitan region, he recovered more than nine thousand six hundred qing of land that the Prince of Cheng, Zhu Yunzhen, and others had encroached upon.

sentences.zh: 張居正疾篤，疏薦其座主潘晟入內閣，帝從之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng was gravely ill he memorialized recommending his patron Pan Sheng for the Grand Secretariat; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng lay gravely ill, he memorialized recommending his patron Pan Sheng for the Grand Secretariat, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 國與同官魏允貞、雷士楨及給事中王繼光、孫煒、牛惟炳、張鼎思抗言不可，寢其命。

translations.literal: Guo, together with his colleagues Wei Yunzhen and Lei Shizhen and supervising secretaries Wang Jiguang, Sun Wei, Niu Weibing, and Zhang Dingsi, protested that this could not be done, and the order was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Guo, together with his colleagues Wei Yunzhen and Lei Shizhen and supervising secretaries Wang Jiguang, Sun Wei, Niu Weibing, and Zhang Dingsi, protested that this must not be done, and the order was shelved.

sentences.zh: 已，極論中官馮保罪。

translations.literal: Thereafter he argued at length the offenses of the eunuch Feng Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he argued at length the offenses of the eunuch Feng Bao.

sentences.zh: 且言：「居正死，保令徐爵索其家名琴七、夜光珠九、珠簾五、黃金三萬、白金十萬。

translations.literal: And he said: "After Juzheng's death, Bao ordered Xu Jue to demand from his household seven famous zithers, nine luminous pearls, five pearl curtains, thirty thousand taels of gold, and one hundred thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "After Juzheng died, Bao ordered Xu Jue to demand from his household seven famous zithers, nine luminous pearls, five pearl curtains, thirty thousand taels of gold, and one hundred thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 居正子簡修躬賫至保邸，而保揚言陛下取之，誣汙聖德。

translations.literal: Juzheng's son Jianxiu personally carried them to Bao's residence, yet Bao proclaimed that Your Majesty had taken them, slandering and defiling the sacred virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's son Jianxiu personally carried them to Bao's residence, yet Bao proclaimed that Your Majesty had taken them, thereby slandering the imperial virtue.

sentences.zh: 」因發曾省吾、王篆表裏結納狀。

translations.literal: He thereby exposed the inside-and-out collusion of Zeng Shengwu and Wang Zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby exposed the inside-and-out collusion of Zeng Shengwu and Wang Zhuan.

sentences.zh: 國疏自外至，與李植疏先後上。

translations.literal: Guo's memorial arrived from outside the capital and was submitted shortly after Li Zhi's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Guo's memorial arrived from outside the capital and was submitted shortly after Li Zhi's memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝已納植言罪保，植遂受知，而國亦由此顯名。

translations.literal: The emperor had already accepted Zhi's words and condemned Bao; Zhi thereby won favor, and Guo also became famous from this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already accepted Zhi's words and condemned Bao; Zhi thereby won favor, and Guo also became famous from this affair.

sentences.zh: 還朝，薦王錫爵、陸樹聲、胡執禮、耿定向、海瑞、胡直、顏鯨、魏允貞。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he recommended Wang Xijue, Lu Shusheng, Hu Zhili, Geng Dingxiang, Hai Rui, Hu Zhi, Yan Jing, and Wei Yunzhen.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, he recommended Wang Xijue, Lu Shusheng, Hu Zhili, Geng Dingxiang, Hai Rui, Hu Zhi, Yan Jing, and Wei Yunzhen.

sentences.zh: 尋出督南畿學政，以疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon he went out to supervise education in the southern metropolitan region and returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out to supervise education in the southern metropolitan region and returned home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 起掌河南道。

translations.literal: He was recalled to take charge of the Henan surveillance circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to take charge of the Henan surveillance circuit.

sentences.zh: 首輔申時行欲置所不悅者十九人察典，吏部尚書楊巍等依違其間，國力持不可。

translations.literal: Chief Grand Secretary Shen Shixing wished to place nineteen men he disliked in the inspection register; Minister of Personnel Yang Wei and others wavered between the two sides, but Guo strenuously held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Grand Secretary Shen Shixing wished to place nineteen men he disliked on the inspection blacklist; Minister of Personnel Yang Wei and others wavered, but Guo strenuously held that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 時行以御史馬允登資在國前，乃起允登掌察，而國佐之。

translations.literal: Shixing, because censor Ma Yundeng's seniority predated Guo's, raised Yundeng to take charge of inspections while Guo assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Because censor Ma Yundeng's seniority predated Guo's, Shixing raised Yundeng to take charge of inspections while Guo assisted him.

sentences.zh: 諸御史鹹集，允登書十九人姓名，曰：「諸人可謂公論不容者矣。

translations.literal: When the censors had all assembled, Yundeng wrote out the nineteen men's names and said: "These men may be said to be those whom public opinion will not tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: When the censors had all assembled, Yundeng wrote out the nineteen men's names and said, "These men may be said to be those whom public opinion will not tolerate.

sentences.zh: 」國熟視，叱曰：「諸人獨忤執政耳。

translations.literal: Guo stared closely and shouted: "These men merely offended the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Guo stared closely and shouted, "These men merely offended the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 天日監臨，何出此語！

translations.literal: Heaven and sun oversee all — how can such words be spoken!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and sun oversee all — how can such words be spoken!

sentences.zh: 」允登意不回。

translations.literal: Yundeng's intent did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Yundeng's intent did not change.

sentences.zh: 國怒，奮前欲毆允登。

translations.literal: Guo was angry and lunged forward intending to strike Yundeng.
translations.idiomatic: Guo was angry and lunged forward intending to strike Yundeng.

sentences.zh: 允登走，國環柱逐之，同列救解。

translations.literal: Yundeng fled; Guo chased him around a pillar, and his colleagues intervened to separate them.
translations.idiomatic: Yundeng fled; Guo chased him around a pillar, and his colleagues intervened to separate them.

sentences.zh: 事聞，兩人並調外，國得四川副使。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, both men were transferred outside the capital; Guo received appointment as Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, both men were transferred outside the capital; Guo received appointment as vice commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 而十九人賴國以免。

translations.literal: The nineteen men were spared thanks to Guo.
translations.idiomatic: The nineteen men were spared thanks to Guo.

sentences.zh: 久之，起故官，蒞山西。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was recalled to his former post and took up office in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled to his former post and took up office in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 改督河南學政，遷山東參政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise education in Henan and promoted to Administration Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervise education in Henan and promoted to administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 所在以公廉稱。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he was known for fairness and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he was known for fairness and integrity.

sentences.zh: 召為太仆少卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 復出為山西副使，歷南京通政使。

translations.literal: He went out again as Vice Commissioner of Shanxi and served in succession as Vice Commissioner of Transport at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He went out again as vice commissioner of Shanxi and served in succession as vice commissioner of transport at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，以兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史巡撫保定。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was made Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year (1609) he was made vice minister of war and concurrently right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 歲兇，屢上寬恤事宜。

translations.literal: In years of famine he repeatedly memorialized measures of relief and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine he repeatedly memorialized measures of relief and leniency.

sentences.zh: 大盜劉應第、董世耀聚眾稱王，剽劫遠近，督兵討滅之。

translations.literal: The great bandits Liu Yingdi and Dong Shiyao gathered crowds and styled themselves kings, plundering far and near; he led troops to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: The great bandits Liu Yingdi and Dong Shiyao gathered crowds and styled themselves kings, plundering far and near; he led troops to exterminate them.

sentences.zh: 進右都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief while continuing as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right censor-in-chief while continuing as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 國剛介。

translations.literal: Guo was stern and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Guo was stern and upright.

sentences.zh: 與弟吏部侍郎圖並負時望，為黨人所忌。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Tu, Vice Minister of Personnel, both bore the hopes of the age and were envied by factionalists.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Tu, vice minister of personnel, both bore the hopes of the age and were envied by factionalists.

sentences.zh: 乞休歸，卒。

translations.literal: He begged leave to retire and died.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave to retire and died.

sentences.zh: 余懋衡，字持國，婺源人。

translations.literal: Yu Maohéng, styled Chiguo, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Maohéng, whose style was Chiguo, came from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twentieth year of the Wanli reign (1592).

sentences.zh: 除永新知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 征授御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 時以殿工，礦稅使四出，驕橫。

translations.literal: At the time, because of palace construction, mining-tax commissioners were sent out on four sides and acted with arrogant violence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, because of palace construction, mining-tax commissioners were sent out on four sides and acted with arrogant violence.

sentences.zh: 懋衡上疏言：「與其騷擾裏巷，榷及雞豚，曷若明告天下，稍增田賦，共襄殿工。

translations.literal: Maohéng memorialized, saying: "Rather than harass lanes and alleys and levy taxes even on chickens and pigs, how much better to make clear to all under Heaven a slight increase in land tax to support palace construction together.
translations.idiomatic: Maohéng memorialized, saying, "Rather than harass lanes and alleys and levy taxes even on chickens and pigs, how much better to make clear to all under Heaven a slight increase in land tax so all may support palace construction together.

sentences.zh: 今避加賦之名，而為竭澤之計，其害十倍於加賦。

translations.literal: Now, to avoid the name of increasing taxes while adopting a plan to drain the pond dry, the harm is ten times that of increasing taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Now, to avoid the name of increasing taxes while adopting a plan to drain the pond dry, the harm is ten times that of increasing taxes.

sentences.zh: 」忤旨，停俸一年。

translations.literal: This offended the imperial will; his salary was suspended for one year.
translations.idiomatic: This offended the imperial will; his salary was suspended for one year.

sentences.zh: 巡按陜西。

translations.literal: He toured and inspected Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He toured and inspected Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 稅監梁永輦私物於畿輔，役人馬甚眾。

translations.literal: Tax commissioner Liang Yong transported private goods through the metropolitan region, impressing very many men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioner Liang Yong transported private goods through the metropolitan region, impressing very many men and horses.

sentences.zh: 懋衡奏之。

translations.literal: Maohéng memorialized against this.
translations.idiomatic: Maohéng memorialized against this.

sentences.zh: 永大恨，使其黨樂綱賄膳夫毒懋衡。

translations.literal: Yong hated him deeply and had his follower Yue Gang bribe the cook to poison Maohéng.
translations.idiomatic: Yong hated him deeply and had his follower Yue Gang bribe the cook to poison Maohéng.

sentences.zh: 再中毒，不死。

translations.literal: Poisoned a second time, he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Poisoned a second time, he did not die.

sentences.zh: 拷膳夫，獲所予賄及余蠱。

translations.literal: Under torture the cook confessed the bribe given him and the remaining poison.
translations.idiomatic: Under torture the cook confessed the bribe given him and the remaining poison.

sentences.zh: 遂上疏極論永罪，言官亦爭論永，帝皆不省。

translations.literal: He then memorialized at length Yong's offenses; censorial officials also argued against Yong, but the emperor took notice of none of it.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized at length Yong's offenses; censorial officials also argued against Yong, but the emperor took notice of none of it.

sentences.zh: 永慮軍民為難，召亡命擐甲自衛。

translations.literal: Yong feared that soldiers and civilians would make trouble and summoned fugitives to don armor in his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yong feared that soldiers and civilians would make trouble and summoned fugitives to don armor in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 御史王基洪聲言永必反，具陳永斬關及殺掠吏民狀。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Jihong openly declared that Yong would certainly rebel and set forth in detail Yong's breaking through passes and killing and plundering officials and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Jihong openly declared that Yong would certainly rebel and set forth in detail Yong's breaking through passes and killing and plundering officials and civilians.

sentences.zh: 巡撫顧其誌頗為永諱，永乃藉口辨。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Gu Qizhi largely covered for Yong, and Yong took this as grounds to argue in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Gu Qizhi largely covered for Yong, and Yong took this as grounds to argue in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝疑御史言不實。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected the censors' words were untrue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected the censors' words were untrue.

sentences.zh: 而鹹寧、長安二知縣持永益急。

translations.literal: Yet the magistrates of Xianning and Chang'an pressed Yong all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the magistrates of Xianning and Chang'an pressed Yong all the more urgently.

sentences.zh: 永黨王九功輩多私裝，恐為有司所跡，托言永遣，乘馬結陣馳去。

translations.literal: Yong's followers Wang Jiugong and others had much private baggage and, fearing officials would track them, claimed to act on Yong's orders, formed ranks, and galloped away on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's followers Wang Jiugong and others had much private baggage and, fearing officials would track them, claimed to act on Yong's orders, formed ranks, and galloped away on horseback.

sentences.zh: 縣棣追及之華陰，相格鬥，已皆被系，懋衡遂以反逆聞。

translations.literal: County assistants pursued and overtook them at Huayin; after fighting they were all seized, and Maohéng then reported rebellion and treason.
translations.idiomatic: County assistants pursued and overtook them at Huayin; after fighting they were all seized, and Maohéng then reported rebellion and treason.

sentences.zh: 永窘甚，爪牙盡亡，獨綱在，乃教永誣劾鹹寧知縣滿朝薦，朝薦被逮。

translations.literal: Yong was in dire straits; his henchmen were all gone, only Gang remained, and he taught Yong to lodge a false impeachment against Xianning magistrate Man Chaojian; Chaojian was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was in dire straits; his henchmen were all gone, only Gang remained, and he taught Yong to lodge a false impeachment against Xianning magistrate Man Chaojian; Chaojian was arrested.

sentences.zh: 永不久亦撤還，關中始靖。

translations.literal: Yong was soon withdrawn as well, and the Guanzhong region at last grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was soon withdrawn as well, and the Guanzhong region at last grew calm.

sentences.zh: 懋衡尋以憂歸。

translations.literal: Maohéng soon returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Maohéng soon returned home on account of mourning.

sentences.zh: 起掌河南道事。

translations.literal: He was recalled to take charge of Henan circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to take charge of Henan circuit affairs.

sentences.zh: 擢大理右寺丞，引疾去。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review and resigned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and resigned on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 李三才，字道甫，順天通州人。

translations.literal: Li Sancai, styled Daofu, was a native of Tongzhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sancai, whose style was Daofu, came from Tongzhou in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Wanli reign (1574).

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue and served through to department director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue and rose through the ranks to department director.

sentences.zh: 與南樂魏允貞、長垣李化龍以經濟相期許。

translations.literal: He and Wei Yunzhen of Nanle and Li Hualong of Changyuan pledged themselves to one another in matters of statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wei Yunzhen of Nanle and Li Hualong of Changyuan pledged themselves to one another in matters of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 及允貞言事忤執政，抗疏直之，坐謫東昌推官。

translations.literal: When Yunzhen spoke on affairs and offended the chief minister, Sancai submitted a forceful memorial in his defense and was demoted to investigating censor of Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunzhen spoke on affairs and offended the chief minister, Sancai submitted a forceful memorial in his defense and was demoted to investigating censor of Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 再遷南京禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to department director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to department director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 會允貞、化龍及鄒元標並官南曹，益相與講求經世務，名籍甚。

translations.literal: When Yunzhen, Hualong, and Zou Yuanbiao were all serving in the southern ministries, they increasingly joined in pursuing affairs of governing the age, and their fame spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunzhen, Hualong, and Zou Yuanbiao were all serving in the southern ministries, they increasingly joined in pursuing affairs of governing the age, and their fame spread widely.

sentences.zh: 遷山東僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Administration Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 所部多大猾積盜，廣設方略，悉擒滅之。

translations.literal: The territory under his charge had many great rascals and long-accumulated bandits; he laid out many stratagems and captured and exterminated them all.
translations.idiomatic: The territory under his charge had many great rascals and long-accumulated bandits; he laid out many stratagems and captured and exterminated them all.

sentences.zh: 遷河南參議，進副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administration Commissioner of Henan and promoted to Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administration commissioner of Henan and promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 兩督山東、山西學政，擢南京通政參議，召為大理少卿。

translations.literal: He twice supervised education in Shandong and Shanxi, was promoted to Participating Secretary of the Nanjing Office of Transmission, and was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He twice supervised education in Shandong and Shanxi, was promoted to participating secretary of the Nanjing Office of Transmission, and was summoned as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以右僉都御史總督漕運，巡撫鳳陽諸府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, concurrently Grand Coordinator of Transport, and Grand Coordinator of the prefectures of Fengyang and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1599) he was made right vice censor-in-chief, concurrently grand coordinator of transport, and grand coordinator of the prefectures of Fengyang and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 時礦稅使四出。

translations.literal: At the time mining-tax commissioners were sent out on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: At the time mining-tax commissioners were sent out on four sides.

sentences.zh: 三才所部，榷稅則徐州陳增、儀真暨祿，鹽課則揚州魯保，蘆政則沿江邢隆，棋布千里間。

translations.literal: In the territory under his charge, tax monopoly was exercised by Chen Zeng at Xuzhou and Ji Lu at Yizhen, salt tax by Lu Bao at Yangzhou, and reed administration by Xing Long along the river — spread like chess pieces across a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the territory under his charge, tax monopoly was exercised by Chen Zeng at Xuzhou and Ji Lu at Yizhen, salt tax by Lu Bao at Yangzhou, and reed administration by Xing Long along the river — spread like chess pieces across a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 延引奸徒，偽鍥印符，所至若捕叛亡，公行攘奪。

translations.literal: They drew in wicked followers, forged seals and tallies, and wherever they went it was as if hunting rebels and fugitives, openly seizing and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: They drew in wicked followers, forged seals and tallies, and wherever they went it was as if hunting rebels and fugitives, openly seizing and plundering.

sentences.zh: 而增尤甚，數窘辱長吏。

translations.literal: Zeng was especially severe, repeatedly shaming senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng was especially severe, repeatedly shaming senior officials.

sentences.zh: 獨三才以氣淩之，裁抑其爪牙肆惡者，且密令死囚引為黨，輒捕殺之，增為奪氣。

translations.literal: Only Sancai confronted him with spirit, checked his henchmen who committed outrages, and secretly ordered condemned prisoners to be drawn into their faction and then seized and killed — Zeng's arrogance was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Only Sancai confronted him with spirit, checked his henchmen who committed outrages, and secretly ordered condemned prisoners to be drawn into their faction and then seized and killed — Zeng's arrogance was broken.

sentences.zh: 然奸民以礦稅故，多起為盜。

translations.literal: Yet because of mining taxes wicked commoners in many places rose up as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of mining taxes wicked commoners in many places rose up as bandits.

sentences.zh: 浙人趙一平用妖術倡亂。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang man Zhao Yiping used sorcery to incite rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang man Zhao Yiping used sorcery to incite rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事覺，竄徐州，易號古元，妄稱宋後。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered he fled to Xuzhou, changed his name to Gu Yuan, and falsely claimed descent from the Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was discovered he fled to Xuzhou, changed his name to Gu Yuan, and falsely claimed descent from the Song.

sentences.zh: 與其黨孟化鯨、馬登儒輩聚亡命，署偽官，期明年二月諸方並起。

translations.literal: With his followers Meng Huajing, Ma Dengru, and others he gathered fugitives, appointed bogus officials, and set the second month of the coming year for simultaneous risings in all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: With his followers Meng Huajing, Ma Dengru, and others he gathered fugitives, appointed bogus officials, and set the second month of the coming year for simultaneous risings in all quarters.

sentences.zh: 謀泄，皆就捕。

translations.literal: When the plot leaked out, all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked out, all were captured.

sentences.zh: 一平亡之寶坻，見獲。

translations.literal: Yiping fled to Baodi and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Yiping fled to Baodi and was seized.

sentences.zh: 三才再疏陳礦稅之害，言：「陛下愛珠玉，民亦慕溫飽；

translations.literal: Sancai again memorialized on the harm of mining taxes, saying: "Your Majesty loves pearls and jade; the people also long for warm clothing and full bellies;
translations.idiomatic: Sancai again memorialized on the harm of mining taxes, saying, "Your Majesty loves pearls and jade; the people also long for warm clothing and full bellies;

sentences.zh: 陛下愛子孫，民亦戀妻孥。

translations.literal: Your Majesty loves sons and grandsons; the people also cherish wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty loves sons and grandsons; the people also cherish wives and children.

sentences.zh: 奈何陛下欲崇聚財賄，而不使小民享升鬥之需；

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty wish to amass wealth and bribes while not letting common people enjoy their measure of grain;
translations.idiomatic: Why should Your Majesty wish to amass wealth and bribes while not letting common people enjoy their measure of grain;

sentences.zh: 欲綿祚萬年，而不使小民適朝夕之樂。

translations.literal: You wish to extend the dynasty for ten thousand years, yet will not let common people enjoy their daily pleasures.
translations.idiomatic: You wish to extend the dynasty for ten thousand years, yet will not let common people enjoy their daily pleasures.

sentences.zh: 自古未有朝廷之政令、天下之情形一至於斯，而可幸無亂者。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has never been a time when court ordinances and the condition of all under Heaven had reached such a point and one could still hope for no disorder.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity there has never been a time when court ordinances and the condition of all under Heaven had reached such a point and one could still hope for no disorder.

sentences.zh: 今闕政猥多，而陛下病源則在溺誌貨財。

translations.literal: Today governmental deficiencies are many, but the root of Your Majesty's illness lies in drowning the will in love of goods and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Today governmental deficiencies are many, but the root of Your Majesty's illness lies in drowning the will in love of goods and wealth.

sentences.zh: 臣請渙發德音，罷除天下礦稅。

translations.literal: Your servant begs that a gracious edict be broadly issued to abolish mining taxes throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant begs that a gracious edict be broadly issued to abolish mining taxes throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 欲心既去，然後政事可理。

translations.literal: Once desire is removed, then government affairs may be set in order.
translations.idiomatic: Once desire is removed, then government affairs may be set in order.

sentences.zh: 」逾月未報，三才又上言：「臣為民請命，月余未得請。

translations.literal: More than a month passed without response; Sancai again spoke, saying: "Your servant pleaded for the people's lives, yet for more than a month has received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month passed without response; Sancai again spoke, saying, "Your servant pleaded for the people's lives, yet for more than a month has received no answer.

sentences.zh: 聞近日章奏，凡及礦稅，悉置不省。

translations.literal: I hear that recently, of all memorials touching on mining taxes, none have been heeded.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that recently, of all memorials touching on mining taxes, none have been heeded.

sentences.zh: 此宗社存亡所關，一旦眾畔土崩，小民皆為敵國，風馳塵騖，亂眾麻起，陛下塊然獨處，即黃金盈箱，明珠填屋，誰為守之？

translations.literal: This concerns the survival or destruction of the altars of state; once the multitude rebels and the realm crumbles, common people all become enemy states, wind-driven dust swirls, and rebellious crowds rise like hemp — Your Majesty sits alone as a block; even if gold fills chests and luminous pearls fill the house, who will guard them?
translations.idiomatic: This concerns the survival or destruction of the altars of state; once the multitude rebels and the realm crumbles, common people all become enemy states, wind-driven dust swirls, and rebellious crowds rise like hemp — Your Majesty sits alone as a block; even if gold fills chests and luminous pearls fill the house, who will guard them?

sentences.zh: 」亦不報。

translations.literal: Again no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Again no response was given.

sentences.zh: 三十年，帝有疾，詔罷礦稅，俄止之。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the emperor fell ill; an edict abolished mining taxes, but soon it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1602) the emperor fell ill; an edict abolished mining taxes, but soon it was halted.

sentences.zh: 三才極陳國勢將危，請亟下前詔，不聽。

translations.literal: Sancai argued at length that the nation's situation was about to grow perilous and begged that the earlier edict be issued at once; this was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Sancai argued at length that the nation's situation was about to grow perilous and begged that the earlier edict be issued at once; this was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 清口水涸阻漕，三才議浚渠建閘，費二十萬，請留漕粟濟之。

translations.literal: The Qingkou River dried up and blocked the grain transport; Sancai proposed dredging the channel and building sluice gates at a cost of two hundred thousand, asking to retain transport grain to fund it.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingkou River dried up and blocked the grain transport; Sancai proposed dredging the channel and building sluice gates at a cost of two hundred thousand, asking to retain transport grain to fund it.

sentences.zh: 督儲侍郎趙世卿力爭，三才遂引疾求去。

translations.literal: Supervising Storage Vice Minister Zhao Shiqing argued forcefully against this; Sancai then pleaded illness and begged to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Storage Vice Minister Zhao Shiqing argued forcefully against this; Sancai then pleaded illness and begged to leave.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其委避，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor hated his shirking responsibility and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated his shirking responsibility and permitted it.

sentences.zh: 淮揚巡按御史崔邦亮、巡漕御史李思孝、給事中曹於汴、御史史學遷、袁九臯交章乞留。

translations.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Cui Bangliang of Huai-Yang, Transport Surveillance Commissioner Li Sixiao, supervising secretaries Cao Yubian, Shi Xueqian, and Yuan Jiugao, and censors all submitted linked memorials begging him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Cui Bangliang of Huai-Yang, Transport Surveillance Commissioner Li Sixiao, supervising secretaries Cao Yubian, Shi Xueqian, and Yuan Jiugao, and censors all submitted linked memorials begging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 而學遷言：「陛下以陳增故，欲去三才，托詞解其官。

translations.literal: Xueqian said: "Your Majesty, because of Chen Zeng, wishes to remove Sancai and uses words as a pretext to dismiss him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xueqian said, "Your Majesty, because of Chen Zeng, wishes to remove Sancai and uses words as a pretext to dismiss him from office.

sentences.zh: 年來中使四出，海內如沸。

translations.literal: In recent years eunuch commissioners have gone forth on four sides and the realm seethes like a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years eunuch commissioners have gone forth on four sides and the realm seethes like a cauldron.

sentences.zh: 李盛春之去以王虎，魏允貞之去以孫朝，前漕臣李誌之去亦以礦稅事。

translations.literal: Li Shengchun left because of Wang Hu; Wei Yunzhen left because of Sun Chao; the former transport official Li Zhi also left over mining-tax affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shengchun left because of Wang Hu; Wei Yunzhen left because of Sun Chao; the former transport official Li Zhi also left over mining-tax affairs.

sentences.zh: 他監司守令去者，不可勝數，今三才復繼之。

translations.literal: Other surveillance officials, magistrates, and prefects who left cannot be counted; now Sancai follows in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Other surveillance officials, magistrates, and prefects who left cannot be counted; now Sancai follows in succession.

sentences.zh: 淮上軍民以三才罷，欲甘心於增，增避不敢出。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians on the Huai, because Sancai was dismissed, wished to take satisfaction on Zeng; Zeng did not dare go out.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians on the Huai, because Sancai was dismissed, wished to take satisfaction on Zeng; Zeng did not dare go out.

sentences.zh: 三才不當去可知。

translations.literal: That Sancai ought not to leave is clear.
translations.idiomatic: That Sancai ought not to leave is clear.

sentences.zh: 」疏仍不答。

translations.literal: The memorial again received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial again received no answer.

sentences.zh: 三才遂去淮之徐州。

translations.literal: Sancai then went to Xuzhou on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Sancai then went to Xuzhou on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 連疏請代，未得命。

translations.literal: He submitted linked memorials asking for a replacement but received no order.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted linked memorials asking for a replacement but received no order.

sentences.zh: 會侍郎謝傑代世卿督儲，復請留。

translations.literal: It happened that Vice Minister Xie Jie replaced Shiqing in supervising storage and again asked that Sancai be retained.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Vice Minister Xie Jie replaced Shiqing in supervising storage and again asked that Sancai be retained.

sentences.zh: 乃命三才供事俟代者，帝亦竟不遣代也。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to continue serving until a replacement arrived; the emperor in the end also did not send a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to continue serving until a replacement arrived; the emperor in the end also did not send a replacement.

sentences.zh: 明年九月，復疏言：「乃者迅雷擊陵，大風拔木，洪水滔天，天變極矣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year he again memorialized, saying: "Recently thunderbolts struck the imperial tombs, great winds uprooted trees, and floodwaters rose to the sky — heavenly changes have reached their extreme.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the following year he again memorialized, saying, "Recently thunderbolts struck the imperial tombs, great winds uprooted trees, and floodwaters rose to the sky — heavenly changes have reached their extreme.

sentences.zh: 趙古元方磔於徐，李大榮旋梟於亳，而睢州巨盜又復見告，人離極矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Guyuan was just dismembered at Xu, Li Darong was soon exposed at Bo, and a great bandit of Suizhou was again reported — human separation has reached its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guyuan was just dismembered at Xu, Li Darong was soon exposed at Bo, and a great bandit of Suizhou was again reported — human separation has reached its extreme.

sentences.zh: 陛下每有征求，必曰『內府匱乏』。

translations.literal: Whenever Your Majesty makes a demand, you always say 'the inner treasury is depleted.'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Your Majesty makes a demand, you always say 'the inner treasury is depleted.'

sentences.zh: 夫使內府果乏，是社稷之福也，所謂貌病而天下肥也。

translations.literal: If the inner treasury were truly depleted, that would be the fortune of the altars of state — what is called the face sick while all under Heaven grows fat.
translations.idiomatic: If the inner treasury were truly depleted, that would be the fortune of the altars of state — what is called the face sick while all under Heaven grows fat.

sentences.zh: 而其實不然。

translations.literal: But in fact it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: But in fact it is not so.

sentences.zh: 陛下所謂匱乏者，黃金未遍地，珠玉未際天耳。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty calls depletion is that gold has not yet covered the ground and pearls and jade have not yet reached the sky.
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty calls depletion is that gold has not yet covered the ground and pearls and jade have not yet reached the sky.

sentences.zh: 小民饔飧不飽，重以征求，箠楚無時，桁楊滿路，官惟丐罷，民惟請死，陛下寧不惕然警悟邪！

translations.literal: Common people cannot fill their morning and evening meals, and on top of this come demands; beatings are unceasing, cangues fill the roads, officials only beg dismissal, and the people only beg death — will Your Majesty not be startled into vigilance!
translations.idiomatic: Common people cannot fill their morning and evening meals, and on top of this come demands; beatings are unceasing, cangues fill the roads, officials only beg dismissal, and the people only beg death — will Your Majesty not be startled into vigilance!

sentences.zh: 陛下毋謂臣禍亂之言為未必然也；

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not think your servant's words of calamity and disorder are not yet necessarily so;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not think your servant's words of calamity and disorder are not yet necessarily so;

sentences.zh: 若既已然矣，將置陛下何地哉！

translations.literal: if they are already so, where will Your Majesty be placed!
translations.idiomatic: if they are already so, where will Your Majesty be placed!

sentences.zh: 」亦不報。

translations.literal: Again no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Again no response was given.

sentences.zh: 既而睢盜就獲，三才因奏行數事，部內晏然。

translations.literal: Soon the Suizhou bandits were captured; Sancai thereupon memorialized carrying out several measures, and within his jurisdiction all was calm.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Suizhou bandits were captured; Sancai thereupon memorialized carrying out several measures, and within his jurisdiction all was calm.

sentences.zh: 翕人程守訓以貲官中書，為陳增參隨。

translations.literal: The man of Xi, Cheng Shouxun, bought office as Secretariat Drafter and served as Chen Zeng's aide.
translations.idiomatic: The man of Xi, Cheng Shouxun, bought office as Secretariat Drafter and served as Chen Zeng's aide.

sentences.zh: 縱橫自恣，所至鼓吹，盛儀衛，許人告密，刑拷及婦孺。

translations.literal: He ran rampant as he pleased; wherever he went there were drums and music, magnificent guards of honor; he permitted people to inform secretly, and torture extended even to women and children.
translations.idiomatic: He ran rampant as he pleased; wherever he went there were drums and music, magnificent guards of honor; he permitted people to inform secretly, and torture extended even to women and children.

sentences.zh: 畏三才，不敢至淮。

translations.literal: He feared Sancai and did not dare come to the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He feared Sancai and did not dare come to the Huai.

sentences.zh: 三才劾治之，得贓數十萬。

translations.literal: Sancai impeached and punished him, obtaining bribes of several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sancai impeached and punished him, obtaining bribes of several hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 增懼為己累，並搜獲其奇珍異寶及僭用龍文服器。

translations.literal: Zeng feared this would implicate him and also searched out his rare treasures and regalia bearing dragon designs used in usurpation of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng feared this would implicate him and also searched out his rare treasures and regalia bearing dragon designs used in usurpation of rank.

sentences.zh: 守訓及其黨俱下吏伏法，遠近大快。

translations.literal: Shouxun and his faction were all sent down to the law officers and executed; near and far were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxun and his faction were all sent down to the law officers and executed; near and far were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，皇孫生。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year the imperial great-grandson was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year (1606) the imperial great-grandson was born.

sentences.zh: 詔並礦稅，釋逮系，起廢滯，補言官，既而不盡行。

translations.literal: An edict combined mining taxes, released those in custody, raised the dismissed and stagnant, and filled censorial posts — yet afterward not all were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict combined mining taxes, released those in custody, raised the dismissed and stagnant, and filled censorial posts — yet afterward not all were carried out.

sentences.zh: 三才疑首輔沈一貫尼之，上疏陰詆一貫甚力。

translations.literal: Sancai suspected Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan of obstructing it and memorialized, covertly denouncing Yiguan with great force.
translations.idiomatic: Sancai suspected Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan of obstructing it and memorialized, covertly denouncing Yiguan with great force.

sentences.zh: 繼又言：「恩詔已頒，旋復中格，道路言前日新政不過乘一時喜心，故旋開旋蔽。

translations.literal: He then also said: "The gracious edict has been promulgated, yet is immediately blocked in the middle; travelers say the recent new policies were only riding a moment's joy, and so were opened and then shut again.
translations.idiomatic: He then also said, "The gracious edict has been promulgated, yet is immediately blocked in the middle; travelers say the recent new policies were only riding a moment's joy, and so were opened and then shut again.

sentences.zh: 」又謂：「一貫慮沈鯉、朱賡逼己。

translations.literal: He also said: "Yiguan feared Shen Li and Zhu Geng would press him.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Yiguan feared Shen Li and Zhu Geng would press him.

sentences.zh: 既忌其有所執爭，形己之短，又恥其事不由己，欲壞其成。

translations.literal: He both resented that they would hold to their views and expose his shortcomings, and was shamed that affairs did not proceed from himself, wishing to ruin their success.
translations.idiomatic: He both resented that they would hold to their views and expose his shortcomings, and was shamed that affairs did not proceed from himself, wishing to ruin their success.

sentences.zh: 行賄左右，多方蠱惑，致新政阻格。

translations.literal: He bribed those around the throne and by many means deluded and confused, causing the new policies to be obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed those around the throne and by many means deluded and confused, causing the new policies to be obstructed.

sentences.zh: 」帝得疏，震怒。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial he was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received the memorial he was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 嚴旨切責，奪俸五月。

translations.literal: A stern edict sharply reproved him and docked five months' salary.
translations.idiomatic: A stern edict sharply reproved him and docked five months' salary.

sentences.zh: 其明年，暨祿卒。

translations.literal: The next year Ji Lu died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ji Lu died.

sentences.zh: 三才因請盡撤天下稅使，帝不從，命魯保兼之。

translations.literal: Sancai thereupon asked to withdraw all tax commissioners throughout the empire; the emperor did not assent and ordered Lu Bao to take charge as well.
translations.idiomatic: Sancai thereupon asked to withdraw all tax commissioners throughout the empire; the emperor did not assent and ordered Lu Bao to take charge as well.

sentences.zh: 是時顧憲成裏居，講學東林，好臧否人物。

translations.literal: At this time Gu Xiancheng lived in retirement, lecturing at the Donglin Academy, fond of praising and blaming men.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Gu Xiancheng lived in retirement, lecturing at the Donglin Academy, fond of praising and blaming men.

sentences.zh: 三才與深相結，憲成亦深信之。

translations.literal: Sancai was deeply bound to him, and Xiancheng also deeply trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Sancai was deeply bound to him, and Xiancheng also deeply trusted him.

sentences.zh: 三才嘗請補大僚，選科道，錄遺佚。

translations.literal: Sancai once asked to fill high offices, select censorate and surveillance commissioners, and record the departed and neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Sancai once asked to fill high offices, select censorate and surveillance commissioners, and record the departed and neglected.

sentences.zh: 因言：「諸臣只以議論意見一觸當途，遂永棄不收，要之於陛下無忤。

translations.literal: He thereby said: "The various ministers were only because discussion and opinion once offended those in power forever cast aside and not taken back — in sum they were not disloyal to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby said, "The various ministers were only because discussion and opinion once offended those in power forever cast aside and not taken back — in sum they were not disloyal to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 今乃假天子威以錮諸臣，復假忤主之名以文己過。

translations.literal: Now they borrow the Son of Heaven's authority to imprison the various ministers, and again borrow the name of offending the ruler to adorn their own faults.
